extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants, PTO officials, and congressional/policy staff
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts statutory standards and procedural requirements in the America Invents Act (H.R.1249) governing patentability timing (first-to-file), post-grant and inter partes reviews, derivation and prior-user proceedings, oath/declaration requirements, fee authority, and related PTO procedures and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First inventor to file / effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an invention’s priority date its effective filing date; move the United States to the first-to-file system. New section 102(b) preserves the grace period so that disclosures by the inventor (or disclosures made after the inventor disclosed to the public) during the year prior to filing will not render the invention unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend Sec. 100 to include “effective filing date”; conform Sec. 103 and other provisions to first-to-file; repeal interference proceedings and create derivation proceedings. Sense of Congress that first-to-file promotes constitutional purposes and harmonization with other patent systems. Studies by SBA and USPTO required on effects of first-to-file and on prior user rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceeding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant requesting a derivation proceeding must set forth the basis for finding that an earlier applicant derived the claimed invention and without authorization filed an application claiming such invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be filed within 1 year of the date of first publication of an application for a claim that is substantially the same as the claimed invention. The Patent Trial and Appeal Board determines the right to patent and issues a final decision; decisions may be appealed to the Federal Circuit or to district court under Sec. 146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor’s oath or declaration (substitute statement allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamline the requirement that the inventor submit an oath as part of a patent application and permit an applicant to submit a substitute statement in lieu of the inventor’s oath or declaration in certain circumstances (e.g., inventor unable or unwilling and under obligation to assign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings clause: failure to comply will not be a basis for invalidity or unenforceability if remedied by a supplemental and corrected statement. False substitute statements are subject to same penalties as false oaths. Section 118 amended to allow the assignee or a person with sufficient proprietary interest (or an agent) to file to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-user defense expanded and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior-use defense may be asserted against any patent (not just methods) if the person asserting the defense reduced the subject matter to practice and commercially used it at least 1 year before the effective filing date of the patent (or earlier if patentee invoked the Sec. 102(b) grace period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense cannot be asserted if the subject matter was derived from the patent holder or persons in privity, or if developed pursuant to a funding agreement under Chapter 18 or by a university/technology-transfer organization that did not receive private business funding. The defense may be asserted only by the person who performed or caused the acts to establish the defense (or entities in control relationships); except as part of an ancillary transfer of the entire enterprise/line of business, the right cannot be licensed, assigned, or transferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review availability and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review may be sought on any invalidity ground during the first 12 months after a patent is issued or reissued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant review is a court-like proceeding in which both challenger and patent owner present information. The proceeding may be used to challenge any invalidity ground and may be instituted only if the petition, if not rebutted, shows it is more likely than not that a claim would be found invalid, or if the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question important to other patents or applications. Post-grant petitioners are estopped only for issues they actually raised in the post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes review availability and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review may be sought on the basis of patents and printed publications any time after a post-grant review is concluded or, if no such review is instituted, after the time for seeking such review has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes is limited to prior-art patents and printed publications and may not be instituted unless the petition and response show there is a reasonable likelihood that a claim would be found invalid. Inter partes petitioners are estopped from raising in subsequent Office proceedings any issue they raised or reasonably could have raised, and are also estopped from raising such issues in civil litigation or ITC proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for review shall explain the basis for seeking review, shall identify the petitioner’s real parties in interest and privies, and shall be made publicly available as soon as is practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may file a response explaining why a review should not be instituted. The Director may allow other petitioners to join proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standards: inter partes vs post-grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for instituting reviews differ: inter partes review requires that the information in the petition and response show a reasonable likelihood that a claim would be found invalid; post-grant review requires that the petition, if not rebutted, shows it is more likely than not that a claim would be found invalid, or that it raises a novel or unsettled legal question important to other patents or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These differing thresholds govern whether the Board will institute the respective proceedings; they affect strategic timing and grounds for petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits and interaction with civil litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review must be sought by a party within 12 months of the date when the party is served with a complaint for infringement. Review may not be instituted if the petitioner has previously filed a civil action challenging the patent’s validity (though a declaratory-judgment action may be filed and is automatically stayed until patent owner countersues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent owner sues for infringement within 3 months of the patent’s issue, a pending petition for post-grant review or the institution of such a proceeding may not serve as grounds for staying a court’s consideration of the owner’s motion for a preliminary injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel effects between Office proceedings and litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes and post-grant petitioners are estopped from raising in a subsequent Office proceeding any issue that they raised or reasonably could have raised in the inter partes or post-grant review. Inter partes petitioners are also estopped from raising in civil litigation or an ITC proceeding any issue they raised or could have raised in inter partes review. Post-grant petitioners are estopped in civil litigation or ITC only for issues they actually raised in the post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel rules differ between the two review types, affecting future litigation and administrative strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to join, consolidate, and limit repeated proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may allow other petitioners to join an inter partes or post-grant review, may consolidate multiple proceedings or matters concerning the same patent, and may decline requests for repeated proceedings on the same question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director’s discretion is a gatekeeping tool to promote efficiency and avoid duplicative or abusive proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rulemaking and protections (Director-prescribed regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that make the file in proceedings public; define standards for instituting reviews; allow submission of additional information; establish and govern review and its relationship to other proceedings; set a time limit for requesting joinder in inter partes review; set standards for discovery; prescribe sanctions for abuse; provide for protective orders for confidential information; allow the patent owner to file a response after an inter partes review has been instituted; allow the patent owner to amend the patent; provide either party a right to an oral hearing; and set a 1-year time limit for completion of the proceeding with a 6-month extension for good cause, and provide the petitioner at least one opportunity to file written comments after institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prescribing regulations, the Director shall consider the integrity of the patent system and the efficient operation of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner amendment rights in review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may submit one amendment with a reasonable number of substitute claims, and additional amendments either as agreed to by the parties for settlement, for good cause shown in post-grant review, or as prescribed in regulations by the Director in inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations will govern the form and timing of amendments; amendments tied to settlement do not trigger estoppel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The challenger shall have the burden of proving unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard applies in the instituted post-grant and inter partes proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and estoppel carve-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to settle review proceedings, in which case estoppel shall not apply and a copy of the settlement agreement shall be filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of settlement agreement preserves public record and affects whether estoppel will bind the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall issue a final written decision and a certificate cancelling, confirming, or incorporating claims. A party dissatisfied with a final written decision may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final written decision and certificate are the Office's closing actions; appeals go to the Federal Circuit (or district court in certain contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination to consider and correct information
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a procedure that would allow patent holders to request that PTO review an existing patent to consider, reconsider, or correct information believed to be relevant to the patent; if this supplemental review raises a new question of patentability, PTO would then reexamine the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination is intended to allow patentees to cure issues; CBO estimated related costs and noted an amendment precluding supplemental examination by any patent holder who attempts to practice or practices fraud on the USPTO (see committee amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes reexamination amendments (time limits and expanded universe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend inter partes reexamination to expand the universe of patents that could be challenged but also limit the time period during which such a challenge could be raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes intended to streamline and focus reexaminations; implementation details in statute and Director regulations affect scope and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated reexamination based on third-party citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may determine whether to initiate reexamination on the Director’s own initiative based on citations by any person other than the owner of the patent under section 301 or 302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Office authority to act on external information without a formal third-party request for reexamination by that third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO fee-setting authority and reclassification of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO granted permanent authority to collect and spend certain fees, with the ability, after specified public notice and comment periods, to set fee rates at levels sufficient to cover the agency’s operating costs; fees reclassified to be recorded as offsetting receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes permanent extension of previously temporary fee increases and will affect budgetary classification and availability of funds for PTO operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing incentive (paper-filing fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a new fee charged to patent applicants that do not use electronic means to file an application (electronic filing incentive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBO estimated ~5,000 paper applications per year and collections of about $17 million over 2012–2021; such collections are recorded as offsets to direct spending and made unavailable for PTO spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking litigation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Change false marking suits: permit competitors to recover damages for competitive harm caused by false marking, but eliminate the option for individuals to seek fines on behalf of the government by stating that only the United States can sue for a civil penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute further specifies defenses: defendant not liable for false marking if the patent involved either expired within 3 years of the alleged false marking or if the word 'expired' were added to the claim of patent protection. CBO estimated reduced revenues from false marking cases under these changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on patenting certain tax strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibit certain tax strategies from being patented. The prohibition applies to any application pending on the date of enactment and any application submitted after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBO notes uncertainty in estimating costs to applicants who would forgo patents on such tax strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-user defense reporting and study requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a study of prior user rights and require reporting/studies (Small Business Administration and GAO) on first-to-file effects and implementation of Act provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute requires SBA to prepare a study on effects on small businesses and GAO to conduct an implementation study with reports due after enactment (1 year and 4 years respectively).
